questions.q: According to Asprey, what do mitochondria release when you eat poorly?
a: Free radicals linked to degenerative disease
Extra antioxidants that protect the cells
Hormones that speed up the aging process
Proteins that repair damaged tissue
questions.why: Lesson 1 says a lack of antioxidants lets mitochondria release free radicals behind most degenerative illness.

questions.q: What does the summary suggest eating instead of red meat and trans fats?
a: Fish, free-range white meat, olive oil, nuts and salmon
Whole grains, legumes and low-fat dairy
Lean pork, seed oils and soy products
Eggs, butter and full-fat cheese
questions.why: Lesson 1 recommends healthy fats and protein from fish, white meat, olive oil, nuts and salmon.

questions.q: What does the 16:8 method of intermittent fasting involve?
a: Eating within an eight-hour window and fasting for sixteen
Fasting for eight hours and eating for sixteen
Eating sixteen small meals spread over eight hours
Fasting two days a week for sixteen hours each
questions.why: Lesson 2 describes eating for eight hours and going without food for the other sixteen.

questions.q: What sun exposure does Asprey recommend?
a: Ten to twenty minutes a day at sunrise
An hour at midday without any sunscreen
Avoiding direct sunlight at all times
Using sunbeds through the winter months
questions.why: Lesson 2 says early morning sun for 10 to 20 minutes gives vitamin D without overpowering rays.

questions.q: How does the summary say you can regulate hormones without drugs?
a: Through high-intensity interval training with rest days between
Through daily stretching and long walks
Through cutting all carbohydrates for a month
Through sleeping fewer than six hours a night
questions.why: Lesson 3 recommends HIIT but warns to leave recovery time between intense sessions.
